name: Charles Gorintin
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Alan (Paris health insurer); co-founding advisor, Mistral AI
profile: French engineer who co-founded Alan in 2016 with Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve, building a digital health-insurance 'super-app' for companies in France, Spain and Belgium; Alan has raised over €500m and is valued in the billions. Before Alan he led data-science work at Facebook, Instagram and Twitter. Since 2023 he has also been a co-founding advisor to Mistral AI.
interesting_fact: Alan was the first new health insurance company licensed in France since 1986.
deep_cut_fact: At Facebook, Instagram and Twitter he worked on fighting fake accounts, growth and social psychology; he holds three master's degrees (Ponts ParisTech, ML at ENS Paris-Saclay, Financial Engineering at Berkeley Haas). He co-writes the French Substack 'Intelligence Humaine' on AI for HR.
notes: French-American Foundation Young Leader 2022. Mistral AI link is a strong angle for an AI/data-center podcast.

name: Matthew Scullion
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Matillion (stepped down as CEO Aug 2026); lay member of the University of Manchester Board of Governors
profile: Altrincham-born entrepreneur who co-founded Matillion in Manchester in 2011 after 15 years in UK/European IT systems integration (incl. software division director at Imtech ICT). He built Matillion into a cloud data-integration unicorn and led its pivot to 'Maia' AI data automation; in Aug 2026 Girish Pancha became CEO and Scullion stayed on the board.
interesting_fact: Named EY UK Entrepreneur of the Year 2021; Matillion is one of the few Manchester-born software unicorns, with a second HQ in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded his first startup at age 18, then spent fifteen years in commercial IT and software development before starting Matillion.
notes: CEO transition announced 4 Aug 2026 (PR Newswire): 'Building Maia has been the work of the last several years...' Now has more time; good podcast timing. info@ is a general company inbox, not personal.

name: Oren Zaslansky
current_role: Founder & CEO, Flock Freight (San Diego-area shared-truckload freight company)
profile: San Diego native who grew up around the freight business, started a truckload carrier at 21, then ran a brokerage before founding Flock Freight in 2014-15. Flock pools LTL-sized shipments into 'shared truckloads' using software, avoiding hub-and-spoke terminals; it became a $1B+ unicorn and raised a $60M Series E led by O'Neil Strategic Capital in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Flock Freight describes itself as the largest shared-truckload (STL) freight brokerage in the U.S., moving pooled freight on one truck without terminal transfers to cut damage and emissions.
deep_cut_fact: He told Heavy Duty Trucking 'I was born into freight' - his childhood dinner-table talk was freight bills and flatbeds - and he started his own truckload company at age 21.
notes: One listing calls him Founder & Executive Chairman; most 2025-26 sources say Founder & CEO - confirm title. Frequent logistics-podcast guest (Logistics of Logistics, Alejandro Cremades).

name: Jessica McKellar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Pilot.com (moved from CTO to CEO around July 2024, per recent profiles)
profile: MIT-trained software engineer and three-time co-founder (with Waseem Daher and Jeff Arnold): early engineer at Ksplice (sold to Oracle 2011), co-founder of Zulip (sold to Dropbox 2014), then Pilot (2017), a startup bookkeeping, tax and CFO service that reached a $1.2B valuation in 2021. Long-time Python community leader (PSF director 2012-14).
interesting_fact: She was a senior technical advisor for 16 episodes of HBO's 'Silicon Valley', and won the 2013 O'Reilly Open Source Award for her contributions to Python.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT undergrad studying chemistry, she co-authored a 2006 Science paper, 'Triple-Bond Reactivity of Diphosphorus Molecules' (Cummins group). She also co-wrote O'Reilly's 'Twisted Network Programming Essentials' (2nd ed., 2013).
notes: Some directories still list Daher as CEO and McKellar as CTO; a June 2026 podcast and other profiles call her CEO - verify before outreach. info@pilot.com is a general company inbox. Open-source/Python community angle works well.

name: Jonathan Anguelov
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder of Aircall (left operations Sept 2023); co-founder of real-estate investor Aguesseau Capital; investor-juror on M6's 'Qui veut être mon associé ?'
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded cloud-telephony company Aircall in 2014 with Olivier Pailhès, Pierre-Baptiste Béchu and Xavier Durand; he built its sales organisation and US expansion from New York as Aircall became a $1B+ unicorn. Since leaving operations in 2023 he invests in real estate via Aguesseau Capital, angel-invests and appears as a TV investor.
interesting_fact: Raised in foster care in Sucy-en-Brie, he told his rags-to-unicorn story in the autobiography 'Rien à perdre' (Éditions Alisio / Albin Michel, March 2025).
deep_cut_fact: He sold pizzas at 17 and began investing in real estate at 18 with savings from student jobs; those rental investments were his main income during Aircall's early, unpaid years.
notes: Very public in France (TV, book, podcasts). Aircall went through 500 Startups in San Francisco and raised $2.75M seed. contact@aircall.io is a general company inbox; he is no longer operational there, so outreach via his book publisher or Aguesseau Capital may be better.

name: Adrian Aoun
current_role: Former founder & CEO of Forward (shut down Nov 2024); reported co-founder, board member and advisor of a new, as-yet-unnamed startup with ex-Forward leaders
profile: Serial founder: started NLP company Wavii in 2008 (acquired by Google), then worked on Google's AI efforts and as Larry Page's head of special projects, helping found Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs. In 2016 he launched Forward, a tech-driven primary-care company that raised ~$400M (later building AI 'CarePods') before closing in Nov 2024; he has since been backing a new venture.
interesting_fact: Before Forward he was head of special projects for Larry Page at Google/Alphabet, where he founded Sidewalk Labs.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his 'happy place' is the bike ride up Mount Tamalpais ('Hard to imagine a better way to start the day') and that he's never been a big coffee drinker.
notes: Forward closed abruptly in Nov 2024 - avoid dwelling on it. He discussed the wind-down candidly on the 'More or Less' podcast ep. 74. No current company site/press contact found; LinkedIn is likely best route. He has written guest posts for TechCrunch (techcrunch.com/author/adrian-aoun).

name: Mikita Mikado
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PandaDoc (San Francisco / Minsk-origin document automation and e-signature company)
profile: Minsk-born entrepreneur (BSUIR graduate) who, with co-founder Sergey Barysiuk, built Quote Roller in 2011 to automate sales proposals; it became PandaDoc in 2013, raised funding from Kima Ventures, Microsoft Ventures, HubSpot and others, and hit a $1B valuation in 2021. He has run the company from San Francisco since 2013.
interesting_fact: He was featured in Yury Dud's 2020 documentary on Russian-speaking founders in Silicon Valley, which made him a role model for young people pursuing IT careers.
deep_cut_fact: At 19 he first went to the U.S. on a Work and Travel student program, working part-time jobs while teaching himself web design and software development - years before returning to Minsk to build Quote Roller, PandaDoc's predecessor.
notes: PandaDoc about page lists him as CEO; Keith Rabkin also appears (some third-party sites call Rabkin CEO) - confirm current title. Avoid politics: he was outspoken during Belarus 2020 protests (Protect Belarus initiative). Has told a 'berry seller' origin story in podcasts (Mixergy, SaaS Club).

name: Cameron Woodward
current_role: Co-founder (and CMO per 2022 trade press) of Wrapbook, the production payroll/finance platform for film and TV; current title not confirmed
profile: Former owner of the boutique commercial production house Sprinkle Lab who experienced production-payroll pain first-hand, then co-founded Wrapbook in 2018 with CEO Ali Javid, Hesham El-Nahhas and Naysawn Naji. Wrapbook, backed by investors including Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, handles payroll, insurance and accounting for productions and reached a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: He described Wrapbook as 'built as a tech company that offers a payroll service rather than a payroll service' with software bolted on, with 100+ features for crews and productions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he ran the boutique commercial production house Sprinkle Lab, where he learned the 'prickly problems' of paying crews that inspired the company.
notes: Ali Javid is Wrapbook's CEO; Woodward is lower-profile. A third-party profile (standout.work) says he directed the KONY2012 marketing campaign - unverified, use cautiously. No published press email; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Feng Qingfeng
current_role: CEO & Director, Lotus Technology Inc. (Nasdaq: LOT); Senior Vice President, Geely Holding Group
profile: Geely veteran who joined in the 1990s and rose through sales, manufacturing and R&D to become Geely Auto's VP and CTO. Geely made him CEO of Group Lotus in June 2018; he then led the creation and 2024 Nasdaq listing of Lotus Technology, the Wuhan-based luxury EV arm. In 2026 he steered Lotus toward hybrids (the 'For Me' super-hybrid) and away from an all-electric-only plan.
interesting_fact: He told Brunswick Review 'I drive all kinds of cars. Any car I haven't driven, I want to try.'
deep_cut_fact: His Geely career predates the company's car-making: he started in sales and manufacturing, and back in 1999 Geely sold about 10,000 Citroën Fukang cars, before he moved into project-based R&D managing whole new-car programmes from factory build to launch.
notes: Listed as 'founder' by Hurun, but he is a Geely-appointed CEO rather than a classic founder. Name also appears as Qingfeng Feng / Qing Feng Feng. Head of IR: Demi Zhang. Spoke at Hong Kong Web3 Festival April 2026 on AI mobility.

name: Rick McPhee
current_role: Co-founder of Upside (Washington, DC cash-back/offers marketplace); listed as Head of Engineering / Head of Delivery
profile: Engineering executive who co-founded Upside (formerly GetUpside) around 2015-16 with CEO Alex Kinnier and others; the app gives consumers personalized cash back at gas stations, grocers and restaurants and measures incremental profit for brick-and-mortar merchants, and was valued at about $2B. Profiles credit him with prior engineering leadership at Opower and HP's Fortify Software.
interesting_fact: Upside's model pays shoppers cash back funded only by the incremental profit it can prove it drives for physical retailers (gas, grocery, restaurants); users had earned hundreds of millions of dollars in cash back.
notes: Low public profile; Alex Kinnier is Upside's public face/CEO. Prior Opower (energy-efficiency software) SVP Engineering role and Oxford doctorate appear only on aggregators (Crunchbase, MarketScreener) - unverified but a potential energy-podcast angle worth confirming via LinkedIn.

name: Owen Tripp
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Included Health (San Francisco)
profile: Former Accenture health consultant and eBay data leader who co-founded ReputationDefender/Reputation.com (2006), then co-founded Grand Rounds Health (expert second opinions) with Dr. Rusty Hofmann. He led its 2021 merger with Doctor On Demand, rebranded as Included Health, which now offers navigation, virtual care, an AI assistant 'Dot' and, via the 2026 Firefly Health deal, employer health plans.
interesting_fact: He has a hard line on AI in healthcare: he argues incumbents mostly use AI 'to drive increased profit on existing transactions', while Included Health puts its assistant Dot directly in patients' hands with a clinician watching concerning conversations.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he pioneered eBay's approach to using unstructured data to understand buyer behavior, and co-founded online-reputation pioneer Reputation.com (originally ReputationDefender). He studied Spanish and English literature at Trinity College (Hartford) before a Stanford MBA.
notes: Writes guest columns (Fast Company, American Banker). Very active on AI-in-healthcare topics; Included Health published an AI clinical-governance framework June 2026. Education detail (Trinity) is from secondary profiles.

name: Ghazal Alagh
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Innovation Officer, Honasa Consumer Ltd (Mamaearth parent; NSE/BSE-listed)
profile: Chandigarh-raised entrepreneur who co-founded Honasa in 2016 with Varun Alagh, starting with toxin-free baby products under Mamaearth and growing into India's largest digital-first beauty and personal-care house (Mamaearth, The Derma Co, Aqualogica, BBlunt, etc.), which listed in 2023. She leads new product innovation and was a 'Shark' investor on Shark Tank India season 1.
interesting_fact: Known as the 'Mama Shark', she was one of the original investor-judges on Shark Tank India (2021-22).
deep_cut_fact: Her first job was as an NIIT corporate trainer teaching software to companies like Infosys; she is also a trained painter who did an intensive figurative-art course at the New York Academy of Art in 2013 and earlier ran a diet start-up, dietexpert.in.
notes: High-profile in India (TV, Instagram). Honasa is listed, so investor-relations channels also exist via honasa.in. Her quote on the Honasa page: 'Your current best consumers got you here. Your future consumers will fuel your next stage of growth.'

name: Justin DiPietro
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer, Glia (New York; banking AI / digital customer service platform)
profile: Co-founded Glia (originally SaleMove) in 2012 with CEO Dan Michaeli after working with him as a strategy consultant to large enterprises; previously COO. Glia sells AI-powered contact-center and digital customer-service software to banks and credit unions, was valued at about $1B, and in Nov 2026 announced it had passed $100M ARR with positive cash flow.
interesting_fact: Glia announced in November 2026 that it had surpassed $100M in annual recurring revenue while cash-flow positive, driven by 'banking AI' adoption among community banks and credit unions.
deep_cut_fact: A Penn State graduate, he was a consultant working alongside Dan Michaeli on customer and technology strategy before they co-founded the company as SaleMove in 2012.
notes: Low public profile; Dan Michaeli is Glia's public face. No published press email found on glia.com; LinkedIn likely best route. Earlier title was COO; Glia's site now lists him as Chief Strategy Officer & Co-Founder.

name: Johnny Mitrevski
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Scalapay (Milan-based buy-now-pay-later fintech)
profile: Shellharbour-born engineer (UOW telecoms engineering, 2000) who spent over a decade at Nortel Networks in Wollongong and later was a technology manager at Commonwealth Bank. In 2019 he co-founded Scalapay with CEO Simone Mancini after spotting a lack of BNPL options in Italy; it became Italy's first fintech unicorn in Jan 2022 and in 2025 secured €70M from the EIB.
interesting_fact: Scalapay hit unicorn status in January 2022, under three years after founding, and was dubbed the 'Wollongong-founded' unicorn because its tech team was built in the Illawarra while the business runs from Milan.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself 'a child of the public education system' and spent over a decade commuting by local train to Nortel Networks' office on the University of Wollongong campus - where he met future Scalapay engineering colleagues.
notes: Splits time between Wollongong and Milan. No published press email found; Simone Mancini is the public face. University of Wollongong alumni relations has profiled him and could be a warm route.

name: Iman Abuzeid
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Incredible Health (San Francisco nurse-hiring and career platform)
profile: Sudanese-American physician (MD, University College London) and Wharton MBA who worked in healthcare consulting and McKinsey, then health-tech product roles, before co-founding Incredible Health in 2017 with CTO Rome Portlock. The platform matches nurses with hospitals and offers career tools; it reached a $1.65B valuation in 2022, making her one of very few Black women to lead a $1B+ company.
interesting_fact: Forbes named her one of America's Richest Self-Made Women in 2024 (est. ~$350M), and Inc. put her on its 2020 Female Founders 100.
deep_cut_fact: Incredible Health was not her first company: her first startup (2015) didn't take off, and she has said its lessons pushed her to a much more rigorous framework on market size, competition and unique insight before starting Incredible Health (Masters of Scale episode).
notes: Frequent podcast guest (TechCrunch 'Found' ep.1, Masters of Scale, a16z, Wharton Pulse). Trained as a doctor - healthcare workforce/AI angles work well.

name: Jeremy Almond
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Paystand (Scotts Valley/Santa Cruz, CA; B2B payments network)
profile: UC Santa Barbara computer engineer (MBA, UMass) with prior roles at Digital Instruments/Veeco and NYC tech jobs, who founded Paystand in 2013-14 to make business-to-business payments fee-free and digital - 'Venmo for businesses'. Paystand runs a blockchain-enabled B2B payment network, has raised $90M+, and has grown by acquisitions such as Teampay (2024).
interesting_fact: He frames Paystand's mission as building an industry-wide decentralized-finance network for 'midsized, high-growth companies that are generally producing real things', and was inspired partly by the post-2008 loss of trust in banks.
deep_cut_fact: An avid surfer, he chose to base Paystand in Santa Cruz rather than Silicon Valley proper partly for the waves; customers include local Allterra Solar and the San Francisco vintage-toy maker Super7.
notes: Paystand often cited as Santa Cruz County's largest tech startup. Blockchain/DeFi-for-B2B angle. Avoid personal 2008 housing details.

name: Yod Chinsupakul
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, LINE MAN Wongnai (Thailand); also CEO of payments company RLP after LMWN took majority control
profile: Chulalongkorn engineering graduate and UCLA Anderson MBA who co-founded restaurant-review site Wongnai in 2010 with three classmates. After Wongnai merged with LINE's delivery app LINE MAN in 2020 he became CEO of the combined LINE MAN Wongnai, now a Thai unicorn spanning food delivery, restaurant POS/merchant software and payments, reportedly targeting a 2027 IPO.
interesting_fact: Wongnai was inspired by Yelp: as an MBA student at UCLA Anderson he used Yelp constantly to find restaurants and realised Thailand had no equivalent.
deep_cut_fact: In Wongnai's first lean year the founders took on outside jobs to keep the company alive; he has said that if he ever did something besides LINE MAN Wongnai it might be a small wine shop with friends.
notes: Tatler Gen.T honoree (2023; Leaders of Today 2026). Describes himself as a 'national team athlete' competing with foreign platforms; introduced an ESOP early. Deep-cut fact combines lmwn.com history (outside jobs) and Tatler interview (wine shop).

name: Keone Hon
current_role: Co-founder of Monad; co-founder & general manager, Monad Foundation (formerly co-founder & CEO of Monad Labs, now Category Labs)
profile: Former high-frequency trader (quant at GETCO, then ~8 years leading a futures trading team at Jump Trading, then Jump Crypto) who in early 2022 co-founded Monad Labs with James Hunsaker and Eunice Giarta to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-execution EVM layer-1. The company (renamed Category Labs) raised ~$244M+ incl. a $225M Paradigm-led round; Monad mainnet launched 24 Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Monad's MON public sale in Nov 2025 was the first-ever token sale run through Coinbase's Token Sales platform, ahead of mainnet on 24 Nov 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He earned three MIT degrees by 2011 - a B.S. in Computer Science and Math, a Master of Finance and an M.Eng in Computer Science - before building ultra-low-latency trading systems at GETCO and Jump.
notes: Very active on X and crypto podcasts (Edge Podcast, Unlayered, CryptoNews); X handle widely cited as @keoneHD but not verified here. HFT-systems-to-blockchain-infrastructure angle fits a data-center/compute podcast. Title per IQ.wiki (Dec 2024 move to Foundation) - confirm.

name: Rob Woollen
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Sigma Computing (San Francisco cloud analytics/BI)
profile: Princeton computer-science engineer who joined BEA Systems out of college and became chief architect of WebLogic Server, then spent ~7 years at Salesforce (Chatter principal architect, SVP platform product management, CTO of Salesforce Platform and Work.com). As an EIR at Sutter Hill Ventures he co-founded Sigma in 2014 with Jason Frantz, serving as CEO until 2020; Mike Palmer is now CEO.
interesting_fact: Sigma gives business users a spreadsheet-like interface that queries cloud data warehouses directly; its board includes Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner.
deep_cut_fact: He joined BEA straight out of Princeton during its hypergrowth and was chief architect of WebLogic Server; he has said he learned most by joining teams where he was 'amazed at how great everyone else is', and many BEA/Salesforce colleagues later backed or joined Sigma.
notes: Engineer-founder; guest on Zero Prime Podcast ep.27 ('From Unix coder to engineer-founder') and Modern CTO. Do not confuse with a different Rob Woollen associated with Epinions/Yahoo.

name: Eric Vreeland
current_role: Chief Strategy Officer, Polyhedra Network (zero-knowledge proof / zkBridge infrastructure)
profile: Crypto marketing and strategy executive who joined Polyhedra Network in 2024 as Chief Strategy Officer after leading marketing at LayerZero Labs, with earlier roles at People Data Labs and Jobr. Polyhedra builds ZK-proof infrastructure including zkBridge (connecting 25+ chains) and 'verifiable AI'; he is a frequent podcast spokesperson for the company.
interesting_fact: He argues that 'ZK-proofs are the only way blockchain can realize its true vision', and promotes Polyhedra's push into verifiable AI using zero-knowledge proofs.
notes: Hurun lists him as a founder, but CB Insights/Crunchbase name James Zhang (Abner Zhang) as Polyhedra's founder and Vreeland as CSO who joined in 2024 - he is likely an executive, not a co-founder, and may not be UHNW. Princeton economics / Berkeley Haas MBA appear only in a podcast bio (unverified).
